tones.default: Punchy, playful, clean. Small stories and one clear flow.
tones.polished: Serious and restrained. Continuity, real UI, long holds.
tones.yc-parody: The startup-launch genre that yc-parody plays straight. Learn the conventions so you can deliver them with a straight face.
tones.chaotic: Fast and loud, but still edited. The good ones lock the message and make the frame go wild.
tones.deadpan: Calm, dry, text-forward. The premise is the joke; the delivery never winks.
tones.cinematic: Trailer scale. Borrow a film genre or a famous ad, then add a finishing layer.
tones.app-store: Feature-by-feature, real screens, clear user flow.

examples.quote: like it's the hero video on its GitHub README
examples.borrow: Name where the video will live; it sets length, framing and loop. The project's own three-beat tagline ('Give a site. Write a goal. Jev clicks.') was already the storyboard.

examples.quote: use the pig assets on new branch of lovelee to make a 9:16 short story animation
examples.borrow: A tiny story starring the project's own characters and assets, with the app teased only at the end. Works when the product has a mascot or illustrations.

examples.quote: 1. connect your agent 2. your agent fills out your listing and sets up redemption 3. go live!
examples.borrow: When the product is a three-step flow, the three steps are the three highlights. Nothing else needed.

examples.quote: users ask for branded images and see them added to content
examples.borrow: Show the output landing in its real context (the post, the page), not floating on a gradient.

examples.quote: build me a product demo for my site using /brag skill. make sure to emphasize on all features
examples.borrow: A /brag run in the wild. Note the ask was 'all features'; still pick the 2-3 that carry the story and let the rest go.

examples.quote: build a product promo from our own UI, not generic components
examples.borrow: One element that never cuts: it morphs from state to state, driven by a cursor with real clicks and drags, the camera zooming so each state fills the frame, last frame equal to the first so it loops. Everything computed in seek(t). Adapted from @twoclipping's widely remixed UI-states prompt.

examples.quote: Content enters after its container starts morphing and leaves before the next morph so text never overlaps
examples.borrow: The fix for muddy transitions, plus 'Real UI. Real data. No placeholders.' and 'First render one frame per beat as a contact sheet' before the full render.

examples.quote: The story must also work muted.
examples.borrow: Premium developer-tool launch film: exactly 15s, important content kept inside a 9:16-safe centre so one render crops to every platform, sound that resolves on the final frame.

examples.quote: start with a single dot on a black screen and then have multiple windows show up
examples.borrow: A scale journey for dense, multi-panel products: dot to full desktop, zoom out until it is a point in space, back in on mobile, end on the one-line promise.

examples.quote: Use only facts and numbers that are on the site.
examples.borrow: Premium brand rules in one list: three colours and the site's own fonts, one idea per shot, key objects centred, eased motion only, cut on the beat.

examples.quote: very professionally edited, motion-graphics-styled product launch videos that you see people making on Twitter
examples.borrow: The reference genre itself; 8 videos in the collection start from this prompt. Feature, benefit, feature, logo, all with real assets. Deliver these conventions dead straight and the parody does itself.

examples.quote: make a modern slick and punchy video for a modern startup that works on inference
examples.borrow: Fifteen words that two other creators reused in their own prompts. When the register is clear (slick, punchy, modern startup) the brief can be tiny; spend the effort on the claim, not the adjectives.

examples.quote: just hit 1 million monthly visitors after 8 months after launch
examples.borrow: One milestone number as the spine of the whole video. Only use it if the project actually states it.

examples.quote: inspiration is yc videos and claude social videos
examples.borrow: Naming the genre you are imitating does more than a list of adjectives.

examples.quote: Magenta/green may misregister (print offset) by 2–4px on impact frames only.
examples.borrow: Chaos with rules: a locked six-line message in exact order, a strict three-colour palette, three typefaces with fixed jobs, glitches only on impact frames, a 'STOP SCROLLING' cold open, and a loop.

examples.quote: chaotic brain rot video with excellent motion + sound design
examples.borrow: Chaotic still needs a real mix. Vertical, relentless, but the sound is designed, not stacked.

examples.quote: make a brainrot video about the terminal. i can't escape it.
examples.borrow: The chaos comes from a relatable confession about the product, not from random effects.

examples.quote: Make a ODATANO edit that goes hard
examples.borrow: The fan-edit format: hard beat cuts, flash frames, speed ramps, the product as the subject of the edit.

examples.quote: Go ALL OUT and make the most badass video you possibly can
examples.borrow: Fifteen seconds of a live site at maximum energy. Pair this energy with the site's real copy and visuals or it turns generic.

examples.quote: a 45-second silent short film with no dialogue, where sound tells half the story
examples.borrow: Let sound land the jokes so the picture can stay still and straight-faced.

examples.quote: you're defi saver and explaining yourself in 1st person
examples.borrow: The product narrates itself, earnestly, in first person. Hand-drawn stop-motion keeps it humble.

examples.quote: a bug that doesn't want to be fixed
examples.borrow: A one-line absurd premise played completely straight. The humor is in the premise, never in the delivery.

examples.quote: Words have assigned architectural roles.
examples.borrow: Text-forward done right: one line at a time, the type itself becomes the set, and the final line stands on what earlier words built. Good for copy-driven products.

examples.quote: a 20-second title sequence for a Netflix thriller that doesn't exist yet
examples.borrow: Frame the product as a title sequence: credits-style type, slow reveals, one recurring motif.

examples.quote: inspired by Apple 1984 ad, iykyk! avoid the border text or frames!
examples.borrow: Homage to a famous ad gives instant structure and stakes. Also: no border text or frames, a common AI giveaway.

examples.quote: aim for half the speed you'd default to
examples.borrow: One continuous camera over one desktop, no hard cuts, 1.5-3s eased moves, motion blur and light grain. A spinning list that is texture, not text, then lands slowly on the one that matters.

examples.quote: add film grain and CRT effect, make it mesmerizing
examples.borrow: A finishing layer (grain, CRT, halation) turns clean motion into a look. Apply it last, over everything, and keep text legible through it.

examples.quote: every frame and every sound written in code, no image or video models
examples.borrow: A manifesto built on one quoted line. All visuals and sound generated in code, which is exactly the /brag-slim setup.

examples.quote: each feature stays on screen for at least 2.5 seconds
examples.borrow: Real recordings, not mocks; every number on screen comes from them; text kept clear of the TikTok/Instagram UI; each feature breaks out of the phone into the world around it.

examples.quote: with an example of a user creating a chatgpt ads campaign, then connecting their metrics
examples.borrow: One user's journey chained end to end. Each step is a scene, and the chain itself shows the product's range.

examples.quote: The customer's problem, what I do, how it works in 3 steps, one proof point, and my name at the end
examples.borrow: A five-scene structure that fits any product with a clear job to do.

examples.quote: Quero que simule os gastos em estabelecimentos do dia a dia
examples.translation: I want it to simulate spending at everyday places
examples.borrow: Simulate the product in its real-world setting (supermarket, gas station, restaurant) so each feature arrives as a moment from daily life. Vertical.

examples.quote: showing live stats from the website, show that users can play on desktop and mobile and multiple themes
examples.borrow: Real stats plus platform and theme range as quick, clean cards.
